item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is preferable because it adds the required replayable multipart convenience API without changing shared retry behavior. Both candidates fail to route Upload through FilesService.Add and omit source-reader error coverage, but B additionally makes a broad, explicitly forbidden RawClient retry/ownership change.","reasons":["A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name and filename, preserves Add unchanged, and keeps production changes narrowly scoped.","B changes RawClient.Do semantics for every io.ReadSeeker, including seeking readers, changing content length, replay behavior, and preventing the transport from closing underlying ReadClosers. This conflicts with the contract to preserve Add behavior and avoid retry-machinery refactoring.","Both Upload implementations duplicate Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating a direct contract requirement.","B has substantially better validation and replay tests: it uses an os.File, consumes and compares both request bodies, and confirms no request on invalid input. That advantage does not justify its forbidden cross-cutting behavior change."],"risks_a":["The retry test counts attempts but never reads or compares request bodies, so it could pass even if retried uploads are empty.","There are no tests for empty filename, nil content, or multipart source-reader failures.","Upload duplicates Add internals rather than preserving one request/error path through Add."],"risks_b":["The RawClient change expands scope and alters established behavior for all seekable request bodies, contrary to the frozen contract.","GetBody returns wrappers around the same mutable ReadSeeker, creating fragile shared-position semantics outside the narrowly required buffered Upload path.","Upload still bypasses Add despite documentation directing callers toward it for consistent behavior and retries aside, and no source-reader failure test is included."]}
